rationale: Stephen reports this speech as God's own words to Abraham ('God told him...', 'God said'), and the content tracks Genesis 15:13-14 closely: descendants as foreigners, 'enslaved and mistreated four hundred years', and God's judgment on the enslaving nation (BSB). It is not verbatim: Stephen shifts to the third person, and his closing clause, 'they will come forth and worship Me in this place', is not in Genesis 15:14, which reads 'they will depart with many possessions'. Meyer's commentary on Acts 7:6-7 states that this clause 'is entirely wanting in the LXX. and Hebrew, and is an expansion suggested by Exodus 3:12', so the grade is strong rather than explicit: a marked report of Genesis 15:13-14 with a blended ending.
